questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kosi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kosi is known as the **'Sorrow of Bihar'.**
 
• Kosi River:
 
 
• These include the Tamur Koshi originating from the Kanchenjunga area in the east, the Arun River from Tibet, and Sun Koshi from the Gosainthan area farther west. The Sun Koshi's tributaries from east to west are Dudh Koshi, Bhote Koshi, Tamba Koshi, and Indravati Koshi. 
 
• The sources of seven streams of the Kosi are located in snow-covered areas which also receive heavy rainfall.
 
 
• Consequently, a huge volume of water flows with tremendous speed.
 
 
 
• They unite at Triveni north of the Mahabharata Range to form the Kosi.
 
• The river enters the Tarai of Nepal after cutting a narrow gorge in the Mahabharata Range.
 
• The river channel is braided and it shifts its course frequently.
 
• This has resulted in frequent devastating floods and has converted large tracts of cultivable land into the wasteland in Bihar.
 
 
• **Hence, the Kosi River is often referred to as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.**​

• 
 
Pathogen: ***Corynebacterium diphtheriae (Bacteria)***

• 
 
***Plasmodium*** enters the human body as sporozoites (infectious form) through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. 

 
 
• 
 
The parasites initially multiply within the liver cells and then attack the **red blood cells (RBCs)** resulting in their rupture.

 
 
•

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel 'A Passage to India'?

__***Key Points__**

__
 
• A Passage to India* (1924) is a novel by English author E. M. Forster set against the backdrop of the British Raj and the Indian independence movement in the 1920s.
 
• It was selected as one of the 100 great works of 20th-century English literature by the *Modern Library* and won the 1924 James Tait Black Memorial Prize for fiction.

questions.question: Alexander the Great defeated Porus in the Battle of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydaspes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Alexander the Great defeated Porus in the Battle of Hydaspes.

 
 
• The Battle is called the “Battle of Hydaspes” named after the Hydaspes (Jhelum) River in Greek.
 
 
 
• The battle was fought in 326 BC with the king of the Paurava dynasty, located on the banks of the Vitasta (Jhelum) river in the **Punjab region.**
 
• In 326 BC, Alexander invaded India, after crossing the river Indus he advanced towards Taxila.
 
• He then challenged king Porus, ruler of the Paurava kingdom, between the rivers Jhelum and Chenab.
 
• The fight on the banks of the Hydaspes River in India was the closest Alexander the Great came to defeat. His feared companion cavalry was unable to subdue fully the courageous King Porus.
 
• The forces were numerically quite evenly balanced, although Alexander had more cavalry and Porus fielded 200 war elephants.
 
• Following the battle, King Porus was brought before Alexander and was asked how he wished to be treated, Porus replied “Treat me as a king would treat another king”. Impressed, Alexander indeed treated him like a king, allowing him to retain his lands.
 
• In **326 BC**, the army of Alexander approached the boundaries of the Nanda Empire. His army, exhausted from the continuous campaigning and concerned at the prospect of facing yet another gigantic Indian army, demanded that they should return to the west. This happened at the Hyphasis (modern Beas).​

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alexander**

 
 
• He was the king of Macedonia and was popularly known as Alexander the Great.
 
• He was a member of the Argead dynasty and was born in 356 BC.
 
• He succeeded his father, Philip, to the throne of Macedonia at the age of only 20.
 
• He quickly conquered many areas including the **Persian (Iranian) empire.**
 
 
 
• After the Battle of Hydaspes and the resounding victory of his troops at Sakla, he reached the Beas River.
 
• But his** soldiers refused to go further,** as they were afraid of the great Magadha kingdom across the Beas river.
 
• **At that time **the Magadha kingdom was ruled by the **Nanda dynasty and the ruler of the Nanda dynasty was Dhanananda**.
 
 
• Mahapadma Nanda was the founder of the Nanda dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Alexander** marched back and reached **Babylon in 323 BC, where he died at the age of 33.**

questions.question: The 6-digit number 439xy5 is divisible by 125. How many such 6-digit numbers are there?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For divisibility by 125, the last 3 digits of the number must be exactly divisible by 125.

The given number 439xy5 ends with the digit 5.

The 3-digit multiples of 125 that end in 5 are 125, 375, 625, and 875.

This gives exactly 4 possible valid combinations for the digits x and y.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 numbers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The 6-digit number is 439xy5.

The number is perfectly divisible by 125.

**Concept Used:**

A number is divisible by 125 if the number formed by its last three digits is a multiple of 125.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The last three digits of the given number are xy5.

⇒ We need to find all 3-digit multiples of 125.

⇒ The multiples of 125 up to 1000 are: 125, 250, 375, 500, 625, 750, and 875.

⇒ Since the last digit of our specific number is 5, we must eliminate all multiples ending in 0 (which are 250, 500, and 750).

⇒ The remaining possible values for xy5 are 125, 375, 625, and 875.

⇒ This corresponds to 4 different values for the digit pair (x, y).

**∴ The correct answer is 4 numbers.**

A number is divisible by 25 if its last two digits are 00, 25, 50, or 75.

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is exactly divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 125

A number is divisible by 125 if the number formed by its last three digits is a multiple of 125 (e.g., 000, 125, 250, 375, etc.).
